steps.title: Prepare mobile EEG system
steps.instruction: Connect the LiveAmp mobile EEG system (BrainProducts GmbH) to a laptop via Bluetooth, place the unit in the waterproof pocket of the backpack, and ensure the three 8 mm passive surface electrodes, reference and ground leads, SAC2 electrode cream, and Animal Polster adhesive bandage are ready.

steps.title: Shave dorsal head region
steps.instruction: While the broiler (Ross 308) is calmly held on a lap with a hand on the back of the neck, shave the dorsal head directly behind the comb using a cordless Vega GT410 clipper with GT606 head; measure the clipper noise with a PCE‑322A sound level meter; the shaving should take about 30 seconds.

steps.title: Clean shaved area
steps.instruction: Wipe the shaved skin with a swab soaked in 70 % isopropyl alcohol and allow it to dry before electrode placement.

steps.title: Place and fix electrodes
steps.instruction: Apply SAC2 electrode cream to three 8 mm electrodes, position each electrode approximately 0.5 cm behind the comb, and press lightly for at least 1 minute to ensure adhesion; cover the entire head from comb to neck with an Animal Polster adhesive bandage for additional fixation.

steps.title: Record baseline EEG
steps.instruction: Allow the bird to reach a quiet state (no head shaking or wing flapping for 10 seconds), then start a 30‑second baseline recording; the mobile unit’s 3‑axis accelerometer records movement; digitise at 500 Hz, apply a 50 Hz notch filter, and a digital band‑pass filter set to 1 Hz (high‑pass) and 40 Hz (low‑pass) using BrainVision Analyzer 2.3.

steps.title: Document experimental conditions
steps.instruction: Note the following metrics for each animal: time required for electrode placement (<3 min for 10 birds in the facility, 5–10 min in the slaughterhouse), clipper maximum noise level (60 dB), ambient noise (up to 90 dB in the slaughterhouse), distance between laptop and EEG unit (≈1 m), number of birds processed (68 total, 16 with head‑shaking aborts, 52 attempted recordings, 45 successful baseline recordings, 7 with artifacts), and any repeat electrode applications.
